item.title: Japan’s Companies Boost Capital Investment as Profits Surge
item.description: Japanese companies raised capital spending in the second quarter as profits surged, in the latest sign that the corporate sector is coping fairly well with the fallout from the Middle East conflict.

item.title: South Korea’s Exports Gather Pace as Chip Boom Powers Ahead
item.description: South Korea’s exports extended their strong growth in August as artificial-intelligence demand powered chip shipments and the broader economy, giving the central bank little reason to retreat from its newly hawkish stance after back-to-back interest-rate hikes.

item.title: Gold Holds Decline as Mideast Flare-Up Raises Fed Rate-Hike Bets
item.description: Gold steadied after a two-day drop as the US and Iran exchanged strikes for the first time in a month, raising the odds of rising energy costs pushing up inflation and pressuring the Federal Reserve to lift interest rates.

item.title: Anthropic Seals $35 Billion Cloud Deal With Nvidia-Backed Lambda
item.description: Anthropic PBC agreed to a $35 billion computing deal with Lambda, a cloud provider backed by Nvidia Corp., part of an effort to quickly expand its AI capacity, according to a person familiar with the matter.

item.title: Malaysia Bonds Lag Peers in August on Supply, Rate-Hike Concerns
item.description: Malaysian bonds delivered Southeast Asia’s worst performance in August as concern over the supply of long-dated notes and the risk of an interest-rate hike made investors cautious.

item.title: Australia’s Beetaloo Shale Gas Could Power Northern Territory AI Data Centers
item.description: Australia’s Northern Territory started commercial production from the nation’s first shale gas wells, as the sparsely populated region bets on the fossil fuel to power a wave of new data centers.

item.title: US Funds Alcoa Gallium Plant in Australia to Cut China Reliance
item.description: The US Department of War said it will provide $174 million in financing to Alcoa Corp. to build a gallium plant at its alumina refinery in Western Australia, as Washington seeks to reduce its reliance on China for critical minerals.

item.title: UK Shop Price Inflation Hits Two-Year High After Energy Spike
item.description: Prices in British shops rose at the fastest rate in more than two years last month, as the fallout from the Middle East conflict started to filter through to supermarket shelves.

item.title: Bessent Tells Japan Officials Rate Hikes Needed, NHK Says
item.description: US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent told Japanese Finance Minister Satsuki Katayama and Bank of Japan Governor Kazuo Ueda that the Asian country’s next step should be to raise interest rates, NHK reports, citing an interview with a US official.

item.title: Airbnb Rolls Out Pilot Program in US to Lower Fees Paid by Hosts to 6% or 10%
item.description: Airbnb Inc. is testing taking a smaller cut of rental fees from hosts, seeking to fight back against a trend of customers booking directly outside of its platform.

item.title: Asia Data Center Debt Binge Hitting Banks’ Limits, Barclays Says
item.description: The billions of dollars being borrowed to fund data centers in Asia are pushing banks to their limits and making them more selective about which projects to finance, according to senior bankers at Barclays Plc.

item.title: Ares Raises $3.8 Billion for Japan-Focused Logistics Fund
item.description: Ares Management Corp has raised ¥612 billion ($3.8 billion) for its latest Japan-focused logistics development fund, in the largest closed-end institutional fundraise by its real estate business.

item.title: Asian Bonds Under Pressure as Oil Extends Advance: Markets Wrap
item.description: Asian bonds followed Treasuries lower as renewed geopolitical tensions drove oil prices higher, fueling inflation concerns and expectations for further monetary tightening.

item.title: Latest Oil Market News and Analysis for Sept. 1
item.description: Oil rose for a second session as fresh hostilities between the US and Iran raised concerns about prolonged disruptions to energy flows through the Strait of Hormuz.

item.title: Japan Bonds Face Test at 10-Year Sale as Yield Approaches 3%
item.description: Japan’s auction of 10-year government bonds on Tuesday will test demand for this key maturity as yields approach the milestone of 3% and investors position for an interest rate hike from the central bank.

item.title: Australia Raises Wheat Crop Forecast as Export Demand Picks Up
item.description: Australia raised its wheat crop forecast after strong winter rains improved growing conditions, just as the worsening Black Sea crisis creates additional demand for the country’s grain.

item.title: Shein Set to Debut in Test of Investor Demand for Consumer Plays
item.description: Shein Global Holdings Ltd. is set to begin trading in Hong Kong after raising HK$13.6 billion ($1.7 billion) in an initial public offering, testing investor appetite for the stocks of companies outside the artificial intelligence supply chain.

item.title: China Makes Cars So Quickly That Regulators Are Getting Worried
item.description: Chinese automakers’ ambitions to shave even more time off their breakneck development speeds are facing a reality check as regulators ramp up scrutiny of the industry’s safety and testing.

item.title: Hedge Fund Disclosure Deadline Delayed Again by SEC, CFTC
item.description: US regulators delayed for the fourth time additional hedge fund disclosure requirements that are meant to inform agencies about the financial positions of firms during market turbulence.

item.title: Brazil Unveils 2027 Budget With Surplus Target That Markets Doubt
item.description: Brazil’s government unveiled its 2027 budget proposal pledging to deliver a fiscal surplus as investors question whether President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva will tame spending and public debt if he wins reelection.

item.title: Apple Says OpenAI Is Destroying Evidence in Trade Secrets Case
item.description: Apple Inc. escalated its legal battle against OpenAI, claiming in a new court filing that OpenAI is actively destroying crucial evidence and that former iPhone engineer Chang Liu “not only downloaded a confidential Apple circuit schematic but also used it in his work” at the AI company.

item.title: Canada’s Carney Tariff Retaliation Will Hurt Most Industries, Study Warns
item.description: Canada’s planned retaliation against US tariffs may help protect some domestic manufacturers, but it will increase costs and leave many industries worse off, according to a study from Oxford Economics.

item.title: New Zealand Set to Raise Rates Again to Counter Inflation Threat
item.description: New Zealand’s central bank is poised to raise its key interest rate for a second straight meeting as it aims to head off emerging inflationary pressures.

item.title: AI Billionaire-Backed Group Launches Pro-Data Center Ad Blitz
item.description: An advocacy group backed by artificial intelligence industry billionaires is launching a multimillion-dollar ad campaign in election battleground states to try to counter a mounting public backlash against a data center construction wave crucial to the industry’s growth plans.

item.title: Trump’s Latest Tariffs: How He’s Keeping His Trade Wall in Place
item.description: From the start of his second term, US President Donald Trump made clear he would put tariffs at the center of US economic policy. When the Supreme Court invalidated sweeping import duties he imposed citing emergency powers, he used a different provision — Section 122 of the Trade Act of 1974, to set a flat 10% levy on imports. Such tariffs are time-limited, however, and Trump’s expired on July 24.

item.title: Bessent Spoke With Druckenmiller After Mentor Criticized Him
item.description: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said he spoke with Stanley Druckenmiller after his former mentor criticized his recent bond-market intervention, and touted that Treasuries might have outperformed because of that same action.

item.title: Chile Economic Data Disappoint as Storms Add to Copper-Mine Woes
item.description: Chile’s economy kicked off the third quarter with a slew of weaker-than-expected prints as wild winter weather disrupted some mining operations, exacerbating the headwinds facing President José Antonio Kast.

item.title: Nigeria Economy Grows at Fastest Pace in Five Years on Oil Boom
item.description: Nigeria’s economy grew at the fastest pace in five years in the second quarter as elevated crude prices fueled by the US war on Iran boosted output and foreign-currency liquidity.

item.title: India’s Uneven Monsoon Rains Deepen Crop and Inflation Risks
item.description: India’s weaker-than-normal monsoon is threatening key crops, heightening the risk that food prices will rise in the world’s most populous nation.

item.title: Czechs Plan Second-Highest Budget Gap Ever to Boost Investment
item.description: The Czech Republic plans its second-largest budget deficit on record next year as the government seeks to ramp up state investments.
